_help: Wacom Intuos Pro M (PTK670) pad + pen button mapping, read by tablet-pad.py; changes apply without restart.
Profiles are picked by the focused window's class (regex, first match wins, 'default' otherwise).
Pad buttons: left cluster top/right/bottom/left/center = l_top l_right l_bottom l_left l_center,
right cluster = r_top r_right r_bottom r_left r_center. Pen: pen_top (pen_middle / pen_bottom are left to the app).
Actions: {"key": "ctrl+z"} taps, {"hold": "space"} holds while pressed, {"toggle": [a, b], "names": [..]} alternates,
{"mode": "left"|"right"} cycles that dial's modes. Key names are evdev KEY_* without the prefix (ctrl, shift, alt, super ok).
Dial modes: {"name", "cw": action, "ccw": action} or {"name", "scroll": "alt"} (scroll up on clockwise, with those modifiers held).
Or {"name", "pinch": 1.05}: zoom by that factor per detent with a touchpad pinch gesture (GTK apps zoom by exactly that much).
"scribble": action run when a pen stroke is a fast in-place zig-zag (5+ straight passes back over the same spot). In GIMP: undo the scribble
and the stroke before it. "tools": only while a toggle (pen_top) last selected one of these keys (b = paintbrush), so scribbling
with the eraser still erases; keys typed on the keyboard aren't seen, so switch tools with pen_top. Tuning: Stroke in tablet-pad.py.
"unless": skip it while this shell command succeeds: GIMP built with ~/.config/gimp-scribble does real scribble-erase itself.
Optional per cw/ccw mode: "cw_fast"/"ccw_fast" actions, used when the dial is turned quickly (detents < 80 ms apart).
GIMP: use keys, not scroll, for tool options. Scrolls come from a mouse device, so GIMP applies them to the mouse's tool options instead of the pen's.
Zoom: ctrl+scroll and ctrl+alt+shift+d/f step through GIMP's coarse zoom presets; use pinch for fine steps.
Brush size: ctrl+alt+shift+a/s = -/+1 px, c/v = -/+10 px, q/w = halve/double.
The ctrl+alt+shift+q/w/z/x/e/r/d/f keys are GIMP shortcuts for tools-size-*-percent / tools-hardness-* / tools-angle-* / view-zoom-*,
